To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Classically defined, homology cell types differ between rodents and humans by the expression of cell-specific genes; 2) Cell-type specific gene expression and epigentic changes are evident in postmortem human brains; 3) Gender specific transcriptional differences and cell-specific molecular responses occur during aging; and 4) A robust, shared response to an unknown, external event was evident in three donor brains.
